label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Our student-run Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday, after three days of lectures, problems and questions at Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune (5–7 November 2026).

On behalf of my fellow organisers, Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, thank you to everyone who made it possible.

We welcomed 41 MSc and early PhD participants from 9 states, selected from 112 applications on the basis of a statement and one reference. The institute’s student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh supported the school, covering hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Thank you to our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), for the lectures on Mordell–Weil; Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), for modular forms; and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków for computations in Sage. We are grateful to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance and support throughout.

Two moments will stay with me. When the power went out for nearly two hours on the second afternoon and laptop batteries gave up, we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be the best session of the three days.

And when an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Sunanda Iyer’s notes, she corrected it live and thanked him. That openness made it easier for everyone to ask questions.

A special thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm after a booking mix-up, and to the office staff who helped us throughout. Thank you also to our six PhD student volunteers for the TA work and for running the problem sessions so well. That is a format we want to keep.

To all the participants: thank you for the questions, effort and conversations, both inside and outside the sessions. For MSc students especially, a small school can offer something a large conference often cannot: time and space to ask, try, get stuck and ask again.

Slides and problem sheets will be uploaded to the department website within two weeks. We hope to hold a second edition in late 2027, subject to grant funding.
